pathway.title: Primo Brands Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is strong on scale and brand but narrow by product and customer. Net sales were USD 6,797.4 million over the last twelve months, spring water and purified water made up 81.36% of 2025 net sales, one customer was 21% of net sales, and the group runs one segment; scale and more than 80 spring sources, 36 company-owned, support cash-flow visibility, while the concentration means a pricing dispute or a service failure moves a large share of sales. Basis: calculation C12; calculation C25; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86

Leverage is falling but is high, and it rests on add-backs the issuer does not substantiate. Net debt of USD 4,684.7 million is 3.87x reported EBITDA (3.91x with the dividend declared on 2026-11-03, USD 4,728.1 million pro forma), against 3.26x on Adjusted EBITDA and the issuer's own 3.32x; the USD 227.0 million between the two EBITDA measures is 15.81% of Adjusted EBITDA. Since 2026-03-31 last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose by USD 130.4 million and cash by USD 189.2 million while gross debt rose by USD 6.8 million, so deleveraging came from earnings and cash build, not repayment. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C09; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 14

Margins, not sales, are the weak point of 2026. Nine-month net sales rose 2.61% but Adjusted EBITDA fell 0.96%, with a 10.4% fall in the first quarter followed by rises of 5.0% and 1.6%, and gross margin fell 1.22 percentage points, as the rise in transportation costs equalled 79.39% of the rise in net sales. Management cut the bottom of its Adjusted EBITDA range from USD 1,485 million to USD 1,465 million in May 2026 and now expects the lower end, which on the same definition needs fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 363.0 million, 8.65% above a year earlier and well above the best quarter so far. Basis: calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 14

Cash conversion is improving but is flattered by the issuer's own adjusted measure. Free cash flow was USD 319.6 million in nine months 2026 against USD 203.4 million, 32.69% of reported EBITDA, but management's adjusted free cash flow of USD 602.9 million adds back USD 283.3 million of integration, restructuring and other items, USD 101.8 million of which is integration capital spending that rose from USD 84.5 million; payouts took 62.98% of free cash flow, leaving USD 118.3 million. Basis: calculation C08; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C32; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12

Liquidity is adequate and the term loans no longer mature in 2028, but a sizeable note maturity and floating-rate cost remain. The 2028 euro secured notes and the 2029 secured and unsecured notes total USD 1,930.1 million, 38.47% of the instruments in the fair-value table and 1.81 times liquidity, and the term loans are 61.28% of them at SOFR plus 2.75%, so 100 bp adds USD 25.7 million a year today and USD 30.7 million once the USD 500.0 million of swaps have expired by 2027-12-31, against interest cover of 4.05x. Basis: calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C18; calculation C19; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101

Financial policy is the main constraint on the view. Payouts of USD 572.8 million in 2025 were 232.94% of free cash flow, the sponsor's holding is estimated at 26.51% after its August 2026 sale, which probably ended its consent rights over payouts and leverage, and a new USD 300.0 million buyback was approved on 2026-11-03; payouts in 2026 are lower, at 62.98% of free cash flow. Basis: calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C17; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

The primary downside path is cost inflation and service disruption lowering EBITDA while payouts continue. A 10% fall in last-twelve-months reported EBITDA would lift net leverage from 3.87x (3.91x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03) to 4.31x and cut interest cover from 4.05x to 3.64x with net debt unchanged; the revolver's tests of 5.00x first lien net leverage and 2.00x interest cover are well clear of those levels on reported figures, but their definitions are not supplied. Basis: calculation C04; calculation C20; calculation C21; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96

cells.text: Premium spring and sparkling water, purified water, self-service refill water, flavored and enhanced beverages, water dispensers and filtration equipment. Brands include Poland Spring and Pure Life (described as billion-dollar brands), Saratoga, The Mountain Valley, Arrowhead, Deer Park, Ice Mountain, Ozarka, Zephyrhills, Primo Water, Sparkletts, Splash Refresher and AC+ION.

Retail distribution to more than 200,000 outlets; Direct Delivery to homes and businesses; Exchange at about 26,500 retail locations; Refill at over 23,500 self-service stations; water filtration for home and business customers.

More than 50 production facilities, more than 200 depots and a delivery fleet of about 4,800 vehicles. More than 80 spring sources, of which 36 are company-owned, mostly in Maine, Pennsylvania, California, Florida and Texas.
Regional spring water 3,319.9 (49.82%); purified water 2,102.0 (31.54%); premium water 349.9 (5.25%); other water 128.8 (1.93%); other 763.4 (11.46%); total net sales 6,664.0. Reporting unit: US$m.

rows.label: Sales by water type, nine months 2026

cells.text: Regional spring water 2,623.7 (50.04%); purified water 1,640.9 (31.30%); premium water 341.8 (6.52%); other water 94.1 (1.79%); other 542.8 (10.35%); total net sales 5,243.3 against 5,109.9 a year earlier. Reporting unit: US$m.
United States 98.5% and Canada 1.5% of 2025 net sales. No operations outside North America remain after the Israel sale of 2025-10-23.

National and regional grocery, mass-merchandise, drugstore, wholesale and convenience chains in the United States and Canada, plus direct commercial and residential customers. One customer was about 21% of 2025 net sales and 20% of trade receivables.

PET resin, glass, aluminum, HDPE, LDPE, fuel and energy. The group bears commodity cost risk, with supplier pricing agreements and derivatives for some fuel and commodities. In the nine months of 2026, transportation costs added 105.9 and materials costs added 33.0 to cost of sales (US$m).
Water sales are higher in warmer months and working capital needs fluctuate through the year.

Local, regional and national bottled water and beverage companies, filtration providers and large retailers with private-label water. Management describes the group as the category leader in U.S. bottled water by retail market share (Management Language).

Net sales of 1,821.0 in the third quarter (up 3.1%) and 5,243.3 in nine months (up 2.61%); third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of 411.0. Outlook: net sales growth of 2% to 4% at the midpoint, Adjusted EBITDA of 1,465 to 1,515 at the lower end and Adjusted Free Cash Flow of 790 to 810 (US$m).

Exited US Office Coffee Services, which cut nine-month net sales by 21.7 (US$m), and the Eastern Canadian operations; sold Eden Springs UK for 9.7 and Israel for 41.7 net, and the Ontario production facility.

runs.text: The strongest support is scale, brand and a spring-source network that spreads supply risk. Last-twelve-months net sales were USD 6,797.4 million from more than 50 production facilities and more than 80 spring sources, 36 company-owned, so one spring source failing does not stop supply, and the brand portfolio underpins pricing and cash-flow visibility; for creditors this absorbs shocks and underpins refinancing access. Basis: calculation C25; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11

A second support is improving earnings and cash conversion. Free cash flow was USD 319.6 million in nine months 2026 against USD 203.4 million, up 57.13%, and reported EBITDA covered cash interest 4.05x against 3.57x for 2025, which lifts debt service capacity if the improvement holds. Basis: calculation C04; calculation C16; Financial foundation (CP-1)

A third support is liquidity and an extended term loan. Cash and the undrawn revolver total USD 1,064.0 million at 2026-09-30, before the dividend declared on 2026-11-03 whose pro forma effect on cash is not established, the term loans now fall due in 2031 and the revolver in February 2030, so no large maturity falls before the euro notes due 2028-10-31. Basis: calculation C05; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51

A fourth support is reporting quality and a record without priming. The auditor gave an unqualified opinion with effective internal control, quarterly reporting is regular, and the 2025 note exchange and 2026 term loan refinancing are not described as priming or uptier transactions, which supports monitoring and creditor alignment. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91

The most important weakness is financial policy under a falling sponsor stake. Payouts of USD 572.8 million in 2025 were 232.94% of free cash flow, USD 224.1 million of company cash was used beside the three sponsor sell-downs, and the estimated stake of 26.51% probably removed the sponsor's consent rights over payouts, so cash can leave faster than debt is repaid. Basis: calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C26; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The second weakness is margin pressure that has stopped sales growth turning into EBITDA. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA fell 0.96% on net sales up 2.61%, and transport cost growth equalled 79.39% of the sales increase, so deleveraging depends on a margin recovery that the lower end of the guidance already requires in the fourth quarter. Basis: calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 11

The third weakness is leverage that rests on add-backs. Net debt is 3.87x reported EBITDA, or 3.91x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03, and the USD 227.0 million of add-backs behind the lower adjusted figures is unverified, so creditors should underwrite to the reported measure. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The fourth weakness is concentration and service risk: spring water and purified water are 81.36% of sales, one customer is 21%, and a consumer class action alleges missed deliveries after facility closures, so one pricing or service failure can move a large share of sales and cash. Basis: calculation C12; calculation C25; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

The fifth weakness is refinancing and rate exposure: USD 1,930.1 million of notes fall due in 2028 and 2029, and the term loans are floating, so 100 bp adds USD 25.7 million a year today and USD 30.7 million once the swaps expire, while the revolver's springing maturity conditions are not printed. Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C18; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26

cells.text: Primo Brands Corporation, a Delaware corporation organised in 2024 as Triton US HoldCo, Inc. Class A common stock trades on the NYSE as PRMB since 2024-11-11; large accelerated filer; fiscal year ends December 31.
Dual headquarters in Tampa, Florida and Stamford, Connecticut; more than 12,000 associates.
One operating segment, which is also the sole reportable segment; two goodwill reporting units; goodwill of 3,581.9 at 2025-12-31 (US$m).
361,548,061 Class A shares at 2026-11-03; no Class B shares were outstanding at 2026-02-24.
Sponsor Stockholders, controlled by affiliates of One Rock Capital Partners, LLC, held 32.0% of the Class A shares and of the voting power at 2026-02-24; later holding not stated.

Eric J. Foss, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman; David Hass, Chief Financial Officer; Jason Ausher, Chief Accounting Officer; Robert Austin, Chief Operating Officer; Hih Song Kim, Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary.
PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, auditor since 2024; unqualified opinions on the 2025 statements and on internal control over financial reporting; one critical audit matter, insurance reserves.
Moody's: corporate family B1, senior secured Ba3, senior unsecured B3, outlook Positive. S&P: corporate BB-, senior secured BB, senior unsecured B, outlook Neutral.
Net sales of 6,664.0 in 2025 and 5,243.3 in the first nine months of 2026; Adjusted EBITDA of 1,446.8 in 2025, defined by the issuer (US$m).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The 2024 merger created the issuer and its sponsor-controlled starting share register. On 2024-11-08 Primo Water Corporation and Triton Water Parent, Inc. (BlueTriton, the parent of the former Nestlé Waters North America business) became wholly owned subsidiaries of the new parent, Primo Brands Corporation. BlueTriton was the accounting acquirer, former Primo Water holders and the sponsor group owned about 43% and 57% immediately afterwards, and the USD 3,950.3 million purchase price was paid in shares and replacement awards, with goodwill of USD 2,766.5 million, 70.03% of the price. No cash sources and uses or entry multiple is stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147; calculation C27

The 2025 refinancing replaced several instruments in one programme. Exchange offers for the three senior note series drew participation of 99.97%, 98.20% and 99.53%, and the new notes are co-issued by Primo Water Holdings Inc. and Triton Water Holdings, Inc. and guaranteed by the parent and substantially all material wholly owned domestic subsidiaries. On 2025-02-12 the Fourth Amendment repriced the term loans of USD 3,098.6 million principal and added a USD 750.0 million revolver maturing in February 2030, while a USD 350.0 million asset-based facility and Primo Water's prior revolver, which had an initial USD 350.0 million commitment, were repaid and ended. The new secured notes share the term loans' first lien and the 2029 unsecured notes rank below them; holders of original notes who did not tender lost most covenants on all three series and their guarantees on the two secured series, and USD 12.9 million of those notes remains. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 95–98; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C29

On 2026-03-31 the Fifth Amendment refinanced the term loans of USD 3,067.6 million into USD 3,090.0 million maturing in March 2031, at SOFR plus 2.75% with a 0.50% floor and 1.00% a year of amortisation, a net principal increase of USD 22.4 million. This moved the term loan maturity out from March 2028; no maturity schedule printed after the amendment is supplied, so the next large maturities are taken to be the 2028 euro secured notes and the 2029 notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation C30

Equity transactions since the merger moved ownership rather than debt. The sponsor group sold down in three underwritten offerings priced at USD 29.50, USD 31.67 and USD 24.37 per share in 2025-03, 2025-05 and 2026-08, the company received none of the proceeds, and it bought shares alongside each for USD 224.1 million in total. On 2026-11-03 the board declared a dividend of USD 0.12 per share payable 2026-12-04 and approved a new USD 300.0 million repurchase program, both after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101–102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C11

fields.value: The seven supplied filings and releases are enough to support a creditor snapshot of Primo Brands Corp as of 2026-11-05, with covenant, legal-priority and governance conclusions limited by the absence of executed financing documents and the proxy statement. Creditors should treat any such conclusion as resting on the company's own summaries of its debt agreements, not on the agreements themselves.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage runs from the audited 2025 annual report to the third-quarter 2026 report and release published on the as-of date, so the latest balance sheet is dated 2026-09-30. The main source limits are the missing management-reported net leverage at the 2025 year end, a debt maturity schedule that predates the March 2026 term loan refinancing, and earlier history that is not comparable because the 2023 results reflect only one of the two businesses merged in 2024.

Creditors should read the improvement as the roll-off of integration costs plus a cash build of USD 189.2 million since March, which holds only if free cash flow keeps going to cash rather than shareholders.

fields.value: - The filings print a dash, which means nothing was reported, in 7 income statement cells, 36 cash flow cells and 3 balance sheet cells; each is written as not supplied rather than zero. No ratio uses these cells, so nothing is restricted. Severity Low. No action is needed unless the issuer confirms that a dash means nil.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The annual report and the quarterly reports print different line sets, so 6 income statement cells, 78 cash flow cells and 9 balance sheet cells are not printed in the filing for that column; for example proceeds from the sale of property, plant and equipment become a separate line only from the second quarter of 2026 and the 2024 financing items do not recur. This limits line-by-line comparison across columns and nothing else. Severity Low. The action is to compare the subtotals, which are printed in every column.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Net Cash Change is withheld for FY2024, FY2025 and the first quarter, half year and nine months of 2025 because the printed net change includes the cash flows of discontinued operations, which the three activity rows exclude; the printed net change stays in the issuer's own row. This restricts only the cash roll-forward check for 2025. Severity Low. The action is to read the discontinued operations rows beside it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No filing after the annual report prints a debt maturity schedule, so the maturity chart is drawn at 2025-12-31 and still shows USD 3,005.7 million of term loans in 2028 that were extended to March 2031 on 2026-03-31. This restricts any maturity wall or refinancing-window statement as at the cutoff. Severity Medium. The action is to rebuild the post-amendment schedule from the term loan terms and label it derived.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Instrument-level carrying values, finance leases, other debt and the total of unamortized costs are not stated at 2026-09-30, so the debt instruments register cannot reconcile to balance sheet debt and a gap of USD 144.6 million to the fair-value table stays unitemised; the year-end reconciliation is complete. This restricts instrument-level leverage and secured-debt statements at the cutoff. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the quarter's debt note or the issuer's schedule.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management net debt and net leverage at 2025-12-31 are not printed in any source read, because the 2025 results release that carries them is not supplied; the three 2026 quarter-end figures are. This restricts a comparison of year-end leverage with management's own figure. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the 2025 results release.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so covenant definitions, any springing conditions on the revolver, and headroom against the first lien net leverage limit of 5.00 to 1.00 and the interest coverage minimum of 2.00 to 1.00 are not calculable; the issuer reports compliance only. This restricts any covenant or maturity-condition conclusion. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the executed agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer does not state whether each add-back in Adjusted EBITDA is realised, and the bridge amounts reconcile exactly but their classification beyond the issuer's labels is not given. This restricts how far adjusted leverage can be relied on. Severity Medium. The action is to treat the add-backs as unverified and to seek the issuer's classification.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ranking is not stated for finance leases, other debt or the non-tendered original notes, and the revolver's security is stated only through the credit agreement description, so the first three are left out of the debt stack and the revolver is shown with that caveat. This restricts structural-priority statements. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the guarantee and security documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The dividend declared on 2026-11-03 has no stated total, so the cash figure uses the share count of that date; the record-date count may differ. This restricts the pro forma net debt row slightly. Severity Low. The action is to replace it with the paid amount once reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2025-09-30 balance sheet is not in a supplied filing, so no 2025 interim balance is shown beside the 2026 interim balances. This restricts the year-on-year comparison of debt and cash at interim dates. Severity Low. The action is none unless a third-quarter 2025 filing is added.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Per-share data and share counts are not carried in the statement tables, because no credit metric uses them, and the single reporting segment means no segment schedule exists; revenue by water type is in the KPI dashboard instead. This restricts nothing in the ratios. Severity Low. No action is needed.

fields.value: Primo Brands Corp (issuer id prmb), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway: business, ownership, sponsor and governance facts, the 2024 merger and the debt issued or amended since 2025, from the seven supplied filings and news releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Primo Brands is a scaled single-segment water business whose main discretionary risk to creditors is shareholder payouts, and the sponsor's veto over them probably fell away in August 2026, leaving the board and the debt covenants as the only limits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C05; calculation C06; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operations are not the weak point: net sales were USD 6,664.0 million in 2025 and management net leverage fell to 3.32x by 2026-09-30. Payouts are the exposure: 2025 dividends and buybacks of USD 572.8 million were 232.94% of free cash flow of USD 245.9 million, and a new USD 300.0 million buyback program followed on 2026-11-03.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C17; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor control is ending in steps, and the consent rights that let the sponsor restrain payouts most likely lapsed with the August 2026 sale. The sponsor group held 32.0% of the Class A shares on 2026-02-24, and its approval is required for dividends above USD 175.0 million a year, most repurchases and debt that takes total net leverage above 3.5x only while it holds at least 30%. The August 2026 sale and repurchase would leave it near 26.51%, an estimate that assumes those shares came from the group because no filing states the holding. If that holds, the board's own financial policy is the operative restraint on payouts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Company cash has been used to support the sponsor's exits, which is the clearest documented link between company liquidity and the sponsor since the merger. The company bought shares alongside all three sponsor offerings, USD 224.1 million in total, and 52.60% of the buybacks identified for 2025 were tied to sponsor sales; the company received none of the offering proceeds. Creditors bear this only through cash that is not used to repay debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101–102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Payout policy is the swing factor for leverage. In 2025 dividends and buybacks exceeded free cash flow by USD 326.9 million; in the first nine months of 2026 they took USD 201.3 million, or 62.98% of free cash flow of USD 319.6 million. Dividends declared for 2026 come to about USD 175.2 million, level with the USD 175.0 million consent threshold, and the new USD 300.0 million program was approved while management net leverage was 3.32x, under the 3.5x level in the sponsor's consent test, a level that management's own measure exceeded at 3.52x on 2026-03-31, although the agreement's definition may differ.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C34; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2024 merger left a business judged on a short combined record with integration costs still running. Primo Water is consolidated only from 2024-11-09, goodwill is 70.03% of the USD 3,950.3 million purchase price, other integration expenses were USD 55.4 million in the first nine months of 2026, and a consumer class action alleges missed deliveries after facility closures and staff reductions. Earlier-period comparisons therefore mix a 2023 base that holds one of the two businesses with later periods that hold both.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is concentrated by product and customer rather than by segment, and 2026 growth is not yet turning into margin. Regional spring water and purified water were 49.82% and 31.54% of 2025 net sales, one customer was 21% of net sales, and premium water grew 31.66% in the first nine months of 2026; gross profit nevertheless fell by USD 22.6 million on net sales growth of 2.61% as transport and materials costs rose, and management guides 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to the lower end of its range.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C26; calculation C32; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor financing against the shares adds a forced-sale risk that sits outside the group's covenants. Almost all of the sponsor's shares, 99.95% of its 2026-02-24 holding by arithmetic on the stated pledges, back a margin loan and a prepaid variable share forward; a counterparty foreclosure could put shares on the market, and the credit agreement lists a change of control as an event of default and the 2029 unsecured notes carry a put at 101.0% of principal, with the definitions not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C02; calculation C33; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims run through two co-issuing subsidiaries and a broad guarantor group, with the term loans and the secured notes sharing one first lien and the 2029 unsecured notes ranking below them; holders of original notes who did not exchange in 2025 lost most covenants on all three series and their guarantees on the two secured series, and USD 12.9 million of them remains. The March 2026 term loan refinancing moved the term loans from March 2028 to March 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C29; calculation C30; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for control analysis. One person has been both Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman since November 2025, the exemption from independent-board rules ran to 2026-03-11, the 2026 proxy statement, which would show board independence and sponsor designee numbers, is not supplied, and the auditor gave an unqualified opinion with effective internal control at 2025-12-31. Litigation is real but unquantified: a securities class action with a motion to dismiss pending, a consumer class action on delivery service and a long-running label case.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a payout-risk view is that the sponsor may still hold at least 30%, because the 32.0% figure is rounded and the August 2026 shares may not all have come from the group; if so, the consent rights survive. Payouts also look affordable in 2026 at 62.98% of free cash flow, net leverage has fallen to 3.32x, the only distribution made to the sponsor alone, USD 448.6 million, pre-dates the merger, and none of the 2025 or 2026 refinancings is described as a priming, uptier or drop-down. The term loans described at 2025-12-31 also required prepayment from half of excess cash flow, subject to leverage step-downs, although the terms after the March 2026 amendment are not restated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C05; calculation C20; calculation C28; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would soften if a filing or the proxy statement shows the sponsor at or above 30%, if payouts stay below free cash flow after the new program starts, and if net leverage keeps falling toward management's aim. It would harden if payouts exceed free cash flow again, if net leverage rises above 3.5x after buybacks begin, if the sponsor's margin loan or forward is enforced, or if any distribution is funded with new debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed Stockholders Agreement, credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the consent thresholds, restricted-payment baskets and change-of-control definitions rest on the issuer's summaries; this limits the finding that payouts are restrained only by the board and the covenants, which could be stronger or weaker once the documents are read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sponsor's holding after August 2026 is not stated, so the 26.51% figure is derived on the assumption that the shares sold and repurchased came from the 32.0% group; this limits the conclusion that the veto rights lapsed, which is not established until a filing states the holding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied, so the number of sponsor-designated directors, board independence, committee structure and pay are not established; this limits the governance finding to the officer list and the signatures, and it may change the view of how much control the sponsor retains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sponsor's fund vintage, remaining fund life, entry price and equity contribution are not stated, so no exit pressure is inferred from the pattern of sell-downs; this limits the view of sponsor intent to documented actions only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue by channel, customer concentration after 2025 and quantified merger synergies are not stated, so the operating view rests on the water-type mix and one 2025 customer figure; this limits how far margin recovery can be judged from the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2024 merger created the issuer and its sponsor-controlled starting share register. On 2024-11-08 Primo Water Corporation and Triton Water Parent, Inc. (BlueTriton, the parent of the former Nestlé Waters North America business) became wholly owned subsidiaries of the new parent, Primo Brands Corporation. BlueTriton was the accounting acquirer, former Primo Water holders and the sponsor group owned about 43% and 57% immediately afterwards, and the USD 3,950.3 million purchase price was paid in shares and replacement awards, with goodwill of USD 2,766.5 million, 70.03% of the price. No cash sources and uses or entry multiple is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2025 refinancing replaced several instruments in one programme. Exchange offers for the three senior note series drew participation of 99.97%, 98.20% and 99.53%, and the new notes are co-issued by Primo Water Holdings Inc. and Triton Water Holdings, Inc. and guaranteed by the parent and substantially all material wholly owned domestic subsidiaries. On 2025-02-12 the Fourth Amendment repriced the term loans of USD 3,098.6 million principal and added a USD 750.0 million revolver maturing in February 2030, while a USD 350.0 million asset-based facility and Primo Water's prior revolver, which had an initial USD 350.0 million commitment, were repaid and ended. The new secured notes share the term loans' first lien and the 2029 unsecured notes rank below them; holders of original notes who did not tender lost most covenants on all three series and their guarantees on the two secured series, and USD 12.9 million of those notes remains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-03-31 the Fifth Amendment refinanced the term loans of USD 3,067.6 million into USD 3,090.0 million maturing in March 2031, at SOFR plus 2.75% with a 0.50% floor and 1.00% a year of amortisation, a net principal increase of USD 22.4 million. This moved the term loan maturity out from March 2028; no maturity schedule printed after the amendment is supplied, so the next large maturities are taken to be the 2028 euro secured notes and the 2029 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Equity transactions since the merger moved ownership rather than debt. The sponsor group sold down in three underwritten offerings priced at USD 29.50, USD 31.67 and USD 24.37 per share in 2025-03, 2025-05 and 2026-08, the company received none of the proceeds, and it bought shares alongside each for USD 224.1 million in total. On 2026-11-03 the board declared a dividend of USD 0.12 per share payable 2026-12-04 and approved a new USD 300.0 million repurchase program, both after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet.

fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations. The proxy statement, executed financing documents and Stockholders Agreement are not supplied, so control rights rest on the annual report's summaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by an estimated fall in the sponsor stake below the consent threshold and payouts that exceeded free cash flow in 2025, because without sponsor consent rights nothing but the board and the debt covenants limits shareholder returns, which implies slower deleveraging and more reliance on covenant capacity that is not supplied. Countervailing evidence is audited reporting, payouts at 62.98% of free cash flow in 2026 and no stated priming or uptier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sponsor's fund vintage, remaining life, entry price and equity contribution are not stated, and no exit pressure is inferred from vintage. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue by channel, customer concentration after 2025 and quantified merger synergies are not stated in any supplied source. This restricts how far revenue durability and margin recovery can be judged. Severity Medium. The action is to seek channel and customer data from the issuer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The guarantor members and the subsidiary list (exhibit 21.1) are not supplied. This restricts structural priority statements to the issuer's description of the guarantor group. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the exhibit and the indenture guarantor schedules.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The funding source and date within 2024 of the USD 448.6 million sponsor dividend are not stated, and no filing links it to the USD 400.0 million incremental term loans of 2024-03-01. This restricts any conclusion that the distribution was debt funded. Severity Low. The action is to seek the pre-merger financing documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The businesses behind USD 48.0 million of acquisitions in the first nine months of 2026 and USD 29.0 million in 2025 are not described. This restricts any view of acquisition appetite. Severity Low. The action is to check the issuer's filings for the acquired businesses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Loss estimates are not given for the securities class action, the consumer class action or the label case, and the company states it cannot estimate a range. This restricts any view of contingent cash claims. Severity Medium. The action is to track rulings on the pending motions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Open-market purchases by affiliated purchasers in the third quarter of 2026 are not identified. This restricts any view of insider alignment. Severity Low. The action is to check insider filings if needed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2025 repurchase total in the cash flow statement, USD 421.5 million, exceeds the identified repurchases of USD 407.0 million by USD 14.5 million, and the nine-month 2026 total of USD 70.1 million exceeds the program figure of USD 66.6 million by USD 3.5 million; shares withheld for taxes are the likely cause but their value is not stated. This restricts the precision of the payout share tied to sponsor sales. Severity Low. The action is to use the stated figures as shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Primo Brands Corp (issuer id prmb), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway: a fundamental credit view covering the business, financial profile, outlook, downside scenario and monitoring triggers, from the seven supplied filings and releases and the three supplied analyses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Primo Brands is an adequate credit whose improving leverage depends on shareholder payouts staying below free cash flow; creditors should treat financial policy, more than operations, as the swing factor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C10; calculation C11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was 3.87x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, or 3.91x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03, against 4.51x at 2026-03-31; the gain came from earnings and cash rather than repayment, and 2026 margins are under cost pressure. Liquidity of USD 1,064.0 million, with pro forma cash after the dividend not established, and a term loan now due in 2031 leave the 2028 and 2029 notes of USD 1,930.1 million as the refinancing test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C06; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is strong on scale and brand but narrow by product and customer. Net sales were USD 6,797.4 million over the last twelve months, spring water and purified water made up 81.36% of 2025 net sales, one customer was 21% of net sales, and the group runs one segment; scale and more than 80 spring sources, 36 company-owned, support cash-flow visibility, while the concentration means a pricing dispute or a service failure moves a large share of sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; calculation C25; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is falling but is high, and it rests on add-backs the issuer does not substantiate. Net debt of USD 4,684.7 million is 3.87x reported EBITDA (3.91x with the dividend declared on 2026-11-03, USD 4,728.1 million pro forma), against 3.26x on Adjusted EBITDA and the issuer's own 3.32x; the USD 227.0 million between the two EBITDA measures is 15.81% of Adjusted EBITDA. Since 2026-03-31 last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose by USD 130.4 million and cash by USD 189.2 million while gross debt rose by USD 6.8 million, so deleveraging came from earnings and cash build, not repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C09; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins, not sales, are the weak point of 2026. Nine-month net sales rose 2.61% but Adjusted EBITDA fell 0.96%, with a 10.4% fall in the first quarter followed by rises of 5.0% and 1.6%, and gross margin fell 1.22 percentage points, as the rise in transportation costs equalled 79.39% of the rise in net sales. Management cut the bottom of its Adjusted EBITDA range from USD 1,485 million to USD 1,465 million in May 2026 and now expects the lower end, which on the same definition needs fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 363.0 million, 8.65% above a year earlier and well above the best quarter so far.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is improving but is flattered by the issuer's own adjusted measure. Free cash flow was USD 319.6 million in nine months 2026 against USD 203.4 million, 32.69% of reported EBITDA, but management's adjusted free cash flow of USD 602.9 million adds back USD 283.3 million of integration, restructuring and other items, USD 101.8 million of which is integration capital spending that rose from USD 84.5 million; payouts took 62.98% of free cash flow, leaving USD 118.3 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C08; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C32; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and the term loans no longer mature in 2028, but a sizeable note maturity and floating-rate cost remain. The 2028 euro secured notes and the 2029 secured and unsecured notes total USD 1,930.1 million, 38.47% of the instruments in the fair-value table and 1.81 times liquidity, and the term loans are 61.28% of them at SOFR plus 2.75%, so 100 bp adds USD 25.7 million a year today and USD 30.7 million once the USD 500.0 million of swaps have expired by 2027-12-31, against interest cover of 4.05x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C18; calculation C19; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the main constraint on the view. Payouts of USD 572.8 million in 2025 were 232.94% of free cash flow, the sponsor's holding is estimated at 26.51% after its August 2026 sale, which probably ended its consent rights over payouts and leverage, and a new USD 300.0 million buyback was approved on 2026-11-03; payouts in 2026 are lower, at 62.98% of free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C17; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is cost inflation and service disruption lowering EBITDA while payouts continue. A 10% fall in last-twelve-months reported EBITDA would lift net leverage from 3.87x (3.91x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03) to 4.31x and cut interest cover from 4.05x to 3.64x with net debt unchanged; the revolver's tests of 5.00x first lien net leverage and 2.00x interest cover are well clear of those levels on reported figures, but their definitions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C04; calculation C20; calculation C21; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is the speed of the improvement and the cash it produced: net leverage fell 0.64x in two quarters, interest cover is 4.05x against a 2.00x covenant minimum, premium water grew 31.66% and management says Direct Delivery returned to growth earlier than it anticipated. Payouts in 2026 are lower against free cash flow than in 2025, and the issuer's integration cash costs fell to USD 146.3 million from USD 206.2 million. If the add-backs prove one-off and margins recover with freight costs, the credit is stronger than adequate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C02; calculation C16; calculation C22; calculation C23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would weaken if fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA falls short of the USD 363.0 million the guidance needs, if payouts exceed free cash flow again or net leverage on management's measure returns above 3.5x, or if the 2028 euro notes are not refinanced well before 2028-10-31. It would strengthen with filings showing sustained gross margin recovery, debt repayment from free cash flow, a printed maturity schedule after the 2026 amendment, or a sponsor stake confirmed at or above 30%, which would keep its consent rights over payouts in force.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C06; calculation C11; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No maturity schedule or debt note after the 2026-03-31 term loan amendment is supplied, so the size of the 2028 and 2029 refinancing test rests on quarter-end carrying values; this limits the conclusion that the nearest maturities total USD 1,930.1 million, which could differ at principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement's definitions of first lien net leverage and interest coverage are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable; this limits the statement that reported ratios sit well inside the revolver tests to a comparison of stated levels with reported figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer or sector benchmark is supplied, so the business profile is judged against the issuer's own history and statements; this limits the word adequate to issuer-level evidence and does not rank the credit against comparable issuers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no realisation status for its add-backs, so Adjusted EBITDA cannot be verified; this limits any conclusion that leverage is below 3.5x on an adjusted basis and keeps the view anchored on reported EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fourth-quarter results, the 2026 dividend total and the pace of the new buyback are not yet known; this limits the payout conclusion to 2025 and nine months of 2026 and could move the 62.98% figure either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest support is scale, brand and a spring-source network that spreads supply risk. Last-twelve-months net sales were USD 6,797.4 million from more than 50 production facilities and more than 80 spring sources, 36 company-owned, so one spring source failing does not stop supply, and the brand portfolio underpins pricing and cash-flow visibility; for creditors this absorbs shocks and underpins refinancing access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C25; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A second support is improving earnings and cash conversion. Free cash flow was USD 319.6 million in nine months 2026 against USD 203.4 million, up 57.13%, and reported EBITDA covered cash interest 4.05x against 3.57x for 2025, which lifts debt service capacity if the improvement holds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C04; calculation C16; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A third support is liquidity and an extended term loan. Cash and the undrawn revolver total USD 1,064.0 million at 2026-09-30, before the dividend declared on 2026-11-03 whose pro forma effect on cash is not established, the term loans now fall due in 2031 and the revolver in February 2030, so no large maturity falls before the euro notes due 2028-10-31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C05; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A fourth support is reporting quality and a record without priming. The auditor gave an unqualified opinion with effective internal control, quarterly reporting is regular, and the 2025 note exchange and 2026 term loan refinancing are not described as priming or uptier transactions, which supports monitoring and creditor alignment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The most important weakness is financial policy under a falling sponsor stake. Payouts of USD 572.8 million in 2025 were 232.94% of free cash flow, USD 224.1 million of company cash was used beside the three sponsor sell-downs, and the estimated stake of 26.51% probably removed the sponsor's consent rights over payouts, so cash can leave faster than debt is repaid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C26; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is margin pressure that has stopped sales growth turning into EBITDA. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA fell 0.96% on net sales up 2.61%, and transport cost growth equalled 79.39% of the sales increase, so deleveraging depends on a margin recovery that the lower end of the guidance already requires in the fourth quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is leverage that rests on add-backs. Net debt is 3.87x reported EBITDA, or 3.91x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03, and the USD 227.0 million of add-backs behind the lower adjusted figures is unverified, so creditors should underwrite to the reported measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is concentration and service risk: spring water and purified water are 81.36% of sales, one customer is 21%, and a consumer class action alleges missed deliveries after facility closures, so one pricing or service failure can move a large share of sales and cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; calculation C25; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is refinancing and rate exposure: USD 1,930.1 million of notes fall due in 2028 and 2029, and the term loans are floating, so 100 bp adds USD 25.7 million a year today and USD 30.7 million once the swaps expire, while the revolver's springing maturity conditions are not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C18; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Primo Brands sells branded spring, purified, premium and refill water through retail, Direct Delivery, Exchange and Refill, formats that combine consumer retail demand with a recurring delivery and refill base. The recurring formats support cash-flow visibility, but Direct Delivery is also where integration problems surface: a consumer class action alleges missed deliveries after facility closures, and management says only that Direct Delivery returned to growth earlier than it anticipated, with no channel sales supplied. The creditor consequence is that visibility is good in the retail base and unproven in the delivery base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer is a listed holding company whose notes are co-issued by two subsidiaries and guaranteed by the parent and substantially all material wholly owned domestic subsidiaries, with the term loans and secured notes sharing one first lien and the 2029 unsecured notes ranking below. The sponsor group held 32.0% at 2026-02-24 and is estimated at 26.51% after August 2026; sponsor-linked repurchases of USD 224.1 million, a quarterly dividend of USD 0.12 per share and USD 12.9 million of original notes that lost covenants and, on two series, guarantees show a financial policy that favours shareholders at the margin without any documented priming.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; calculation C26; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is largely a consumer staple with a recurring component, and the annual report states that cost increases have historically been recovered through price increases; 2026 tests that, because net sales grew 2.61% in nine months while the increase in transportation costs equalled 79.39% of it. Retail consolidation and private-label water cap pricing power, and one customer is 21% of net sales, so revenue is predictable in volume but not fully in price. Premium water, up 31.66%, is the one line growing fast enough to lift mix.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C13; calculation C23; calculation C25; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The cost base is commodity- and freight-linked: PET resin, aluminum, glass, fuel and energy, with the group bearing the risk and mitigating part through supplier pricing agreements and derivatives, and the filings do not split fixed from variable costs, so operating leverage is not measured. In nine months 2026 cost of sales rose by transportation costs of USD 105.9 million and materials costs of USD 33.0 million, and gross margin fell from 31.12% to 29.90%, so margins are defended mainly by pricing and productivity. Integration costs are fading, with other integration expenses of USD 55.4 million against USD 97.7 million, which helps reported EBITDA more than operating margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C14; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending took 63.85% of operating cash flow in 2025 and 48.89% in nine months 2026, 6.52% and 5.83% of net sales, against base capital spending guided at 4% of net sales; the gap is mostly integration and disaster-related capital spending, USD 101.8 million of it integration in nine months, which should fall away as integration ends. Free cash flow converted 22.73% of reported EBITDA in 2025 and 32.69% in nine months 2026, and the group does not split maintenance from growth capital, so flexibility to cut capital spending in a downturn is real but not measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C16; calculation C27; calculation C28; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high: national and regional beverage companies, retailer private labels and tap-water alternatives compete on brand, price and distribution, which limits price increases. New entry is limited by the cost of replicating a spring-source and depot network, which management calls difficult to replicate, while substitutes, from filtration to municipal water, cap the premium for bottled water. Buyer power is high because retail is consolidated and one customer is 21% of net sales, and supplier power is moderate because some packaging inputs come from few or sole suppliers; the credit effect is a margin ceiling that makes cost pass-through slower than cost inflation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: External factors are a secondary credit driver on the provided materials, with three exceptions that are not quantified in the filings: local bans and taxes on plastic bottles and water extraction, tariff and freight cost pressure, and growing concern about contaminants in public water. They enter the monitoring triggers rather than the base view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Credit strengths are scale, brands, spring-source redundancy, improving cash conversion and liquidity of USD 1,064.0 million at 2026-09-30. Credit weaknesses are leverage that depends on add-backs, margin pressure, concentration by product and customer, and payout policy. The opportunities that could improve credit quality are premium mix, the roll-off of integration costs and capital spending, and EBITDA growth that lowers leverage without repayment; the threats are freight and input cost inflation, plastic and water regulation, retailer pricing pressure, service-failure litigation and the sponsor's pledged shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is adequate and improving. The main supports are scale, brands, liquidity of USD 1,064.0 million with pro forma cash after the 2026-11-03 dividend not established, interest cover of 4.05x and net leverage down to 3.87x, or 3.91x pro forma for that dividend. The main constraints are leverage that rests on USD 227.0 million of add-backs, margins that fell in 2026, payouts that took 232.94% of free cash flow in 2025, and a refinancing test of USD 1,930.1 million in 2028 and 2029. The trend is positive on cash and earnings, and the datapoints still missing are a post-amendment maturity schedule, covenant definitions and the sponsor's current holding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C10; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For the next 12 to 24 months the issuer guides to net sales growth of 2% to 4% and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,465 million to USD 1,515 million, with Adjusted Free Cash Flow of USD 790 million to USD 810 million; the tailwinds are premium mix, Direct Delivery recovery and falling integration costs, and the headwinds are freight and input costs, a fourth-quarter EBITDA step of 8.65% that the guidance needs after the bottom of the range was cut from USD 1,485 million in May 2026, and floating-rate cost as the swaps expire. Over three to five years the credit depends on whether free cash flow goes to debt reduction, which is a policy choice that the sponsor's falling stake leaves to the board.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sector tailwinds are that bottled water is the largest beverage category by volume and a USD 30 billion retail market in 2025, according to the annual report; sector headwinds are plastic regulation, retailer private labels and tariff and freight costs. Company tailwinds are the integration roll-off and a near-term maturity profile pushed to 2028; company headwinds are payout policy, customer concentration and litigation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A realistic downside starts with a freight, resin and aluminum cost spike or a service failure in Direct Delivery that costs volume, while price increases lag. Revenue growth stalls, gross margin falls further from 29.90%, and EBITDA falls; a 10% fall in last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, with net debt unchanged, lifts net leverage from 3.87x (3.91x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03) to 4.31x and cuts interest cover from 4.05x to 3.64x. Free cash flow falls more than EBITDA because interest and capital spending are largely fixed, and if payouts continue at the 2026 rate liquidity of USD 1,064.0 million at 2026-09-30 erodes while leverage stalls above 4x, so the 2028 and 2029 notes are refinanced from a weaker position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C05; calculation C14; calculation C20; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management has levers: the new USD 300.0 million buyback is a ceiling and can be left unused, dividends can be cut from about USD 175.2 million a year, integration capital spending of USD 101.8 million in nine months should end, and base capital spending is guided at 4% of net sales. With those levers resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity problem before 2028; default risk is not assumed from this evidence, and the first reading of stress would be a payout that exceeds free cash flow while net leverage on management's measure is above 3.5x.

fields.value: Basis: calculation C17; calculation C21; calculation C27; calculation C29; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Primo Brands presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, brands and a spring-source network, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that rests on add-backs, margin pressure in 2026 and a payout policy that the sponsor's falling stake no longer checks. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow rose to USD 319.6 million in nine months and interest cover is 4.05x, though adjusted free cash flow overstates it by USD 283.3 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA recovery and on payouts staying below free cash flow before the 2028 euro notes fall due on 2028-10-31, and the primary downside path is cost inflation and service disruption lowering EBITDA while payouts continue. Further analysis would require a printed maturity schedule, covenant definitions, the sponsor's current holding and fourth-quarter results. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: shareholder payouts outpacing free cash flow while margin pressure persists.
